title: RTP: fix RTP Player play failed when SDP not exist
description:
* packet-rtp.c: add conversation info for RTP packets to help RTP Player work
without SDP.

RTP Player in Wireshark *3.4* can playback the rtp-g711 without SDP required, while it's **NOT** work in Wireshark 3.5.

Here are example pcap files, try play the g711 in wireshark:
[rtp-g711-only.pcap](/uploads/0442806892fba82bfaf59e4f20631206/rtp-g711-only.pcap)

If we systematically create the conversation, is this test and the other ones below still necessary?

3.4.X code is similar, so what other change broke the playback and is the systematic creation of a conversation for all RTP packets required?

Your question inspired me to dig more deeper, and for 3.4.x, the player use `rtp_packet->info->info_timestamp`
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/release-3.4/ui/qt/rtp_audio_stream.cpp#L275
while 3.5.x use `rtp_packet->info->info_extended_timestamp`, which maybe not available when conv data is not exist.
https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/ui/qt/rtp_audio_stream.cpp#L340

So the better solution maybe mark the `info_extended_timestamp` is available or not.

I'll check more and upload new commit. Thanks

I implemented info_extended_timestamp to avoid issues with overleaping the counter. The issue is that I missed that counter is part of conversation and it may happen that conversation doesn't exists.

I propose to create conversation just for "Decode as" path, see below.
Hi @pquantin please help review the new commit. Thanks.

It is exactly an issue I found a few days ago. When I use "decode as", conversation is not created and player is not able to play the stream.
I'm just not sure whether this kind of solution is good one. The point is that conversations for RTP are created by other protocols (SIP, ...). So I'm thinking about creating session in "Decode as" path...

Hi @j.novak just initiallize the `extended_timestamp` and `extended_sec_num` with `timestamp` and `sec_num` can resolve the issue.

@sun.lin Yes, but check the code with data with SDP. When conversation is created by upper layer, extended_timestamp starts at 0x100000000 to avoid negative numbers if packets are reordered and first packet if capture is not first packet in RTP stream.

Thank you to spend time on the issue.
extended timestamp is initialized with the timestamp and override later if conversation data is available.

Current change can work with conversation data, or roll back to Wireshark 3.4.x behavior when conversation data not exist.

I strongly suggest approve this commit for 3.5 RC release then got more time for further investigation.
